chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Rayyan ibn Al-Salt, from Yunus, who raised it (to the Imam), said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not send any Prophet at all except that he would have a clear black seal (Mirrah), and Allah did not send any Prophet at all until He affirmed for him the Beginning (Al-Bada').

key_terms.الْبَدَاءِ: The divine manifestation or change in decree
key_terms.مِرَّةٍ سَوْدَاءَ: A clear black seal or mark of prophethood

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the 'black seal' and 'Al-Bada' in the status of Prophets according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the 'clear black seal' (Mirrah) as a distinctive physical mark of prophethood, while linking it to the doctrine of 'Al-Bada'—the divine manifestation of change in destiny—affirmed for every Prophet. This narration underscores the unique ontological status of Prophets in Shia theology, connecting their physical signs with their capacity to embody divine flexibility in decree.

en.hubeali: H 14625 – Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al-Rayyaan Bin Al-Salt, from Yunus who said:

Abu Abdullahasws said that: ‘Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic never Sent a Prophetas at all except that heas would have a clear ‘مِرَّةٍ سَوْدَاءَ’ (Seal of Prophet-hood) and Allahazwj did not Send a Prophetas at all until heas accepts the ‘يُقِرَّ لَهُ بِالْبَدَاءِ’ The Decision of Allah at the Start (About the First ‘Al-Noor’-Mohammedsaww and Ayley Mohammedasws).
en.sarwar: 177. Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al-Rayyaan Bin Al-Salt, from Yunus who said:

Abu Abdullah (a.s.) said that: ‘Allah (azwj) Mighty and Majestic never Sent a Prophet (as) at all except that he (as) would have a clear ‘مِرَّةٍ سَوْدَاءَ’ (Seal of Prophet-hood) and Allah (azwj) did not Send a Prophet (as) at all until he (as) accepts the ‘يُقِرَّ لَهُ بِالْبَدَاءِ’ The Decision of Allah at the Start (About the First ‘Al-Noor’-Mohammed (saww) and Ayley Mohammed (a.s.)).
